title: Replenish line-side bins by their min/max labels
instruction: Replenish the line-side bins by their min/max labels: refill only the bins holding no more parts than their minimum (the red squares on the label) up to exactly their maximum (all the squares) with sockets from the bulk tote, and leave every other bin as it is.
context: Unlike top-up tasks that fill every bin to its max (#328) or add the difference to a par level (#265), this applies a reorder point: each bin's label sets its own min and max, only a bin at or below its min is refilled, to exactly its max, and a bin above its min is left alone, so two bins holding 2 parts need different actions. Material handlers run line-side kanban supply this way to keep stock low without starving the line.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward and y to the left; the table top is 74.75 cm above the floor; everything square to the table. Four blue plastic line-side bins, open-bottomed frames (inside 9 cm in x by 9 cm in y, walls 1 cm thick and 3 cm tall) fixed on the table, centred at x 33 and y 21 (A), 7 (B), -7 (C), -21 (D). In front of each, centred at x 24.25 under the bin's y, lies a white card label (3 cm in x by 9 cm in y, 2 mm thick) with one 1.8 cm square per part of the bin's max, 2.6 cm apart along y, red up to the min and green beyond: A min 1 / max 3, B min 1 / max 3, C min 2 / max 3, D min 1 / max 2. The parts are steel (chrome-vanadium) 3/4-inch drive sockets (NVIDIA SimReady Socket_3_4in_A01: 3.0 cm across, 4.7 cm tall, 90 g), standing on their square-drive end, open end up. A bin's places are at (x, y) offsets (-2.2, -2.2), (-2.2, +2.2) and (+2.2, 0) from its centre, filled in that order: A holds none, B, C and D two each (first two places). A dark grey plastic bulk tote, an open-bottomed frame (inside 6 cm in x by 30 cm in y, walls 1 cm thick and 2 cm tall), is fixed centred at (17, 0) and holds six sockets in a row at x 17, y -12.5, -7.5, -2.5, 2.5, 7.5 and 12.5. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: From a top photo of the end state with the grippers open and clear of the bins. A socket is in a bin when it is released and still, its centre within 3.2 cm of the bin's centre in x and y (inside the walls), and it rests on the bin floor (its underside within 1 cm of the table, not on another socket or a wall), standing or lying. Needed: 3 into A (0, at or below min 1, to max 3) and 1 into C (2, at min 2, to max 3); B (2, above min 1) and D (2, at max 2) need none. Correct: sockets added to A and C, up to those numbers. Mistakes: any change in the count of B or D, a count above max in A or C, and a count below the start in A or C (a socket taken out). Score = 0.25 per correct socket, or 0 if there is any mistake, so possible scores are 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0. Doing nothing, filling every bin to its own max, and one socket into each bin all score 0. Sockets anywhere else (left in the tote, on the table or floor, on a label, still held) count neither way. Success: A 3, B 2, C 3 and D 2, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Put the sockets back so A holds none, B, C and D two each in their first two places, and six in the tote at their marks; any socket works in any place.
fidelity: Approximate. The sockets are NVIDIA SimReady models at real size; bins and tote are fixed open frames on the table rather than bins on a flow rack. The min/max labels show red and green squares instead of printed numbers. Loose objects have rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), higher than steel on plastic, so sockets slip less in the grip than on real arms.
